posts.title: Most people think China only rose by copying the West. History tells the exact opposite story.
posts.description: Many people in the West believe China only became a superpower by copying Western secrets—a myth born out of historical amnesia. Because most schoolbooks focus on the last two centuries of European and American dominance, it is easy to forget that for over a thousand years, China was the richest, smartest, and most inventive civilization on Earth. Before anyone ever accused China of taking ideas from the West, the rest of the world spent centuries borrowing China’s greatest breakthroughs just to catch up. During powerful eras like the Han, Tang, Song, and Ming dynasties, China often generated over a quarter of the entire planet’s wealth through massive trade in silk, tea, and porcelain. At the same time, Chinese inventors led the world in engineering and science, giving humanity game-changing breakthroughs like paper, movable-type printing, gunpowder, the magnetic compass, and the world’s first paper money. posts.title: A Forbidden Love Saved an Empire
posts.description: China, 1854. Nineteen-year-old Robert Hart crosses the world to outrun disgrace and illness, only to collide with a destiny far greater than his shame. In the teeming treaty ports of the Qing Dynasty, he purchased a quiet, perceptive concubine whose language, intuition, and courage open doors he never knew existed. As her whispered guidance leads him past courtiers and cutthroats, Hart learns to read a civilization from the inside out—and to risk everything for the woman who steadies his soul. From the smoke-choked fields of the Taiping Rebellion to the shadow diplomacy of the Opium Wars, Hart navigates treacherous alliances with warring Western powers and wary imperial officials, rising from outcast foreigner to a confidant within the Dragon Throne. posts.title: As a species, humans do not share the same exact genome. The same could be said of different cultures.
posts.description: Any two humans are about 99.9% genetically identical, but that tiny 0.1% variation accounts for millions of differences. The world’s cultures are often described as existing on a spectrum between individualism with a focus on personal goals; independence, and collectivism with its focus on group harmony; loyalty, et al. Then there’s religious influence which acts as a fundamental shaper of culture, deeply embedding values, behavior, and social structures within societies by providing a framework for daily life, morality and identity.
